The Guardian 2 Selvedge is a 14.25oz Japanese selvedge denim developed for strength and durability. The fabric blends cotton with Kevlar®, an aramid fiber developed in 1965 and best known for its exceptional tensile strength, meaning its resistance to tearing and being pulled apart. An interesting fact about Kevlar® is that its discovery was accidental. It was originally developed while researchers were trying to create a lightweight reinforcement fiber for tires. Instead, they produced a fiber so strong and stable that it went on to be used in body armour, aerospace components, and high-performance industrial applications.
Unlike performance fabrics that abandon traditional denim character, Guardian 2 retains the look, feel, and aging potential of classic selvedge denim while offering significantly higher tear resistance than a 100% cotton equivalent. While the jeans are not bulletproof, the Kevlar® content dramatically improves durability in high-stress situations and repeated wear.

The Citrus Kasuri Weft Selvedge is a 14oz Japanese selvedge denim distinguished by its complex weft dyeing technique. Beneath the indigo surface lies a vibrant interior created using traditional Kasuri methods.
Rather than inserting solid-colored weft yarns, Kasuri dyeing involves binding and selectively dyeing sections of yarn before weaving. This results in alternating yellow and green segments along the same yarn, producing organic, patterned coloration rather than uniform stripes.
As the denim wears and abrasions develop, the citrus-toned weft gradually reveals itself through the indigo surface. Due to the labor-intensive nature of Kasuri dyeing, this fabric is used sparingly, making it both expressive and rare.

Being the highest level of recognition awarded by the Leather Working Group, a Gold rating signifies the leather manufacturer meets the most stringent criteria and demonstrates a strong commitment to mitigating its environmental impact.

With a cut inspired by classic American sports overcoats from the 1960s and ’70s, our coach jacket blends functionality with retro style. Similar to a classic windbreaker, this model is designed with a deliberately oversized fit, allowing for ease of movement and heavy layering.
While this style of jacket is traditionally made from nylon to protect against the elements, we’ve opted for a 10oz Japanese nep selvedge denim — creating our most distinctive coach jacket to date. The denim is woven with an indigo rope-dyed warp and a light blue weft, with the neppy warp yarn creating an irregular texture brimming with vintage charm. Unlike many of our denim jackets, this model is partially lined with a 6oz cotton twill — a primarily visual choice intended to conceal the pocket bags — while the back remains unlined to showcase the reverse of the weave.
Other key features include a snap-fastening main opening, a drawstring hem, and ribbed cuffs to reduce wind penetration

p-ironheart-9551654912266.d:
Our relaxed tapered cut jean made from our brand new 14oz broken twill selvedge denim. Broken twill denim was first used in 1964 by Wrangler as a solution for combatting leg twist. The process of weaving fabric in this method sees the combination of both right hand twill (RHT) and left hand twill (LHT) reversed every two warp ends, forming a zigzag-like pattern in the denim and leaving no bias in either direction of the weave, therefore eliminating leg twist.
